headline: MirrorMoE reports improved pretraining for shared-expert MoEs by adapting the routing space
summary: A paper introduces MirrorMoE, a pretraining router for mixture-of-experts models that combines sign-mirrored logits for expert selection with the standard routing probabilities for expert aggregation, then anneals the mirrored component to zero. The authors report that shared experts suppress routing-induced feature variance, while fine-grained experts increase the number of routes that must be explored; in four shared-expert models from 100M to 2.4B total parameters, MirrorMoE lowers test perplexity and improves the average on six commonsense tasks. At 2.4B, the reported changes are 0.67 lower perplexity and +1.64 percentage points in the six-task average. The work uses DCLM data and H100 GPUs; the released recipe identifies one DCLM shard and 90/5/5 train/validation/test split. These are author-reported results at modest scale, not independently reproduced or evidence of frontier-scale gains.
